signature.name: Museum of the Imperial Palace of Manchukuo
signature.detail: The former palace of Puyi, the last emperor of China, who ruled the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo here. It is the city's most important historical site and a must-see for understanding 20th-century China. Tip: go on a weekday morning to avoid crowds; the site is a short taxi ride from the city center.

signature.name: Changchun Film Studio
signature.detail: One of China's oldest and most famous film studios, now a museum dedicated to the country's film history. It is a must for cinema fans and anyone interested in Chinese culture. Tip: check opening hours in advance, as they can vary; it is easily reached by taxi or bus.

signature.name: Jingyuetan National Forest Park
signature.detail: A large forest park with a lake, ideal for hiking, cycling, and escaping the city. It is the best place in Changchun to enjoy nature. Tip: visit in summer or autumn for the best scenery; bring water and snacks as facilities are limited.

signature.name: Changchun World Sculpture Park
signature.detail: A unique park displaying sculptures from around the world, set in a pleasant green space. It is a relaxing and culturally interesting stop. Tip: go in the late afternoon to avoid the heat and enjoy a stroll.

signature.name: Nanhu Park
signature.detail: A popular city park with a lake, gardens, and recreational activities. It is a great spot to experience local life. Tip: visit on a weekend to see locals enjoying the park; entry is free.

food: Casual meal $5-10; mid-range restaurant $15-25 per person
transport: Metro $0.5-1 a ride; taxis cheap, starting at $1.5
